predecessors.name: West Francia
predecessors.text: West Francia, 'ceded to Charles the Bald with the Treaty of Verdun (843)'; 'the accession in 987 of Hugh Capet, Duke of France and Count of Paris, established the Capetian dynasty on the throne'…

successors.name: French First Republic
successors.text: 'on September 21, 1792, the French monarchy was effectively abolished by the proclamation of the French First Republic' (Kingdom of France page)

ledger.x: 987: Hugh Capet is elected king and the Capetian dynasty begins.
990: the Duchy of Aquitaine stands under the crown.
1003: Burgundy leaves the shape for 1003-1017.
1018: Burgundy returns to the shape.
1034: Henry I gives the Duchy of Burgundy to his brother Robert.
1055: the County of Sens is annexed to the royal domain.
ledger.cp: County of Sens (holder not named by the page)

ledger.x: 1068: the crown acquires the Gatinais and Chateau-Landon.
ledger.cp: Gatinais (holder not named by the page)

ledger.x: 1077: the French Vexin is annexed.
1081: Moret-sur-Loing is acquired.
ledger.cp: Moret-sur-Loing (holder not named by the page)

ledger.x: 1101: the Viscounty of Bourges is acquired.
ledger.cp: Viscounty of Bourges (holder not named by the page)

ledger.x: 1138: the duchy's allegiance ends in Cliopatria's relation row (990-1138) as Aquitaine is drawn inside the kingdom from 1139.
1139: Aquitaine is joined to the royal domain under Louis VII.
1152: Aquitaine leaves the royal domain.
1191: Philip II acquires the County of Vermandois.
1191: Artois passes to the Capetian family (given to Prince Louis; integrated into the domain in 1223).
ledger.cp: Artois (holder not named by the page)

ledger.x: 1200: Philip II annexes the Norman Vexin, Evreux and Issoudun.
1204: Philip II confiscates Normandy, Touraine and Anjou from the English crown.
1216: Prince Louis lands in Kent and is proclaimed king in London.
1217: Louis is defeated and leaves England.
1224: Louis VIII conquers Poitou, La Rochelle, Limousin, Perigord and Quercy from the English.
1226: Louis VIII's Languedoc campaign takes numerous cities.
1229: the Treaty of Paris cedes the sénéchaussées of Nîmes to the king after the Albigensian Crusade.
1237: Artois is confirmed as an apanage for the king's brother Robert.
1250: the County of Toulouse passes into the king's family (Alfonso, Count of Poitou, apanage).
1250: Poitou passes into the king's family (Alfonso, Count of Poitou, apanage).
1250: Anjou and Maine pass to a cadet branch (apanage).
1259: the Treaty of Paris leaves the Duchy of Aquitaine to the English king under the crown.
1271: Toulouse, Poitou and Auvergne revert to the crown (the apanages of Alfonso, Count of Poitou).
1284: Champagne is reunited to the royal domain with Philip IV's marriage to Joan I of Navarre.
1284: the County of Chartres is bought for the crown (a second purchase in 1286).
ledger.cp: County of Chartres (seller not named by the page)

ledger.x: 1284: Philip IV marries Joan I and Navarre enters union with the crown.
1301: the Treaty of Bruges makes Bar's county west of the Meuse a French fief.
1305: Limousin cells join the shape.
ledger.cp: Limousin (holder not named by the pages opened)

ledger.x: 1322: Anjou and Valois are reunited with the domain at Charles IV's accession.
1328: the death of Charles IV ends the union with Navarre; Joanna II succeeds.
1328: the House of Valois succeeds the direct Capetians.
1336: Ponthieu is conquered for the crown (given to England in 1360, reattached in 1477).
ledger.cp: County of Ponthieu (holder not named by the page)

ledger.x: 1337: Philip VI confiscates the Duchy of Aquitaine.
1347: Edward III captures Calais, which stays English until 1558.
1349: the Dauphine is bought from the Dauphin of Viennois (transfer 1343-1349).
1356: King John II gives Anjou and Maine to his son Louis, founder of the house of Valois-Anjou.
1360: Ponthieu is given to England.
1360: John, Duke of Berry receives Berry and Auvergne as apanage.
1360: the Treaty of Bretigny cedes enlarged Aquitaine to Edward III (8 May 1360, ratified at Calais in October).
1361: the king claims the Duchy of Burgundy as heir.
1361: the king gives Touraine in appanage to his son Philip (the Bold).
1364: Philip the Bold receives the Duchy of Burgundy in apanage.
1369: Charles V declares the English possessions forfeit and Aquitaine rises.
1380: at Charles V's death the English hold only Calais and a few ports.
1380: Aquitaine is reconquered but for Calais and a few ports.
1402: cells in Guyenne, Orleanais, Gascony and on the Italian coast join the shape.
ledger.cp: Guyenne, Orleanais and Gascony cells (holder not named by the pages opened)

ledger.x: 1407: Auvergne and Languedoc cells join the shape.
ledger.cp: Auvergne and Languedoc (holder not named by the pages opened)

ledger.x: 1417: Henry V takes Caen and begins the conquest of Normandy.
1419: Rouen falls to Henry V (19 January); Normandy is English.
1419: Normandy passes to Henry V.
1422: on Charles VI's death the north goes to Henry VI under the Treaty of Troyes.
1435: the Treaty of Arras returns Paris to the king.
1449: the French retake Rouen and the reconquest of Normandy begins.
1450: victory at Formigny completes the reconquest of Normandy.
1450: Normandy is French again.
1451: Bordeaux surrenders to the French (30 June).
1453: Bordeaux falls for good on 19 October, after Castillon (17 July): the Hundred Years' War ends.
1453: Gascony and Bordeaux are won; only Calais stays English.
1474: Louis XI seizes Anjou after King Rene's will of 22 July 1474.
1476: Louis XI, reconciled to Rene, restores Anjou to him.
1477: Louis XI seizes Burgundy and Picardy after Charles the Bold dies at Nancy (5 January 1477).
Ends with the Bar dossier: "From 1480, it was united to the imperial Duchy of Lorraine" (Duchy of Bar).
July 1480: Rene dies (10 July 1480) and Louis XI 'again added Anjou to the royal domain'.
1481: Charles IV of Anjou dies and leaves his lands to Louis XI.
1481: Provence passes to Louis XI on the death of Charles IV of Anjou, Count of Provence.
1482: the Treaty of Arras annexes Burgundy and Picardy.
1482: Burgundy and Picardy become French.
1482: Franche-Comte and Artois enter the shape.
1491: the personal union of Brittany and the crown begins.
1495: Charles VIII holds Naples.
1495: Ferdinand II regains Naples.
1497: Franche-Comte and Artois leave the shape.
1497: Roussillon leaves the shape.
1499: Louis XII enters Milan (6 October).
1501: Naples is taken (Capua surrenders on 24 July).
1503: the French are expelled from Naples after Garigliano (29 December).
1512: the Swiss retake Milan.
1515: Francis I wins at Marignano and retakes Milan.

November 1521: an Imperial-Papal army under Prospero Colonna and the Marquis of Pescara captures Milan and restores Francesco II Sforza; the French attempt to retake it ends at Bicocca on 27 April 1522.
August 1523: Francis I sequesters the Bourbon lands in dispute after Suzanne's death; Charles III, who signed a treaty with the Emperor in July 1523, breaks with the crown.
1531: the sequestered Bourbon lands are confiscated and annexed (next event).
1531: the possessions of the disgraced Charles III, Duke of Bourbon, are confiscated, after the sequestration of August 1523 (occupation above).
1532: Brittany is united with France.
1532: Brittany joins the kingdom for good.
1536: a French army occupies Turin and Piedmont.
1552: Henry II takes the Three Bishoprics (Treaty of Chambord, January 1552).
1553: a Franco-Ottoman force takes Corsica from Genoa.
1558: the French retake Calais (January).
1559: Cateau-Cambresis (3 April) returns Corsica to Genoa.
1559: Cateau-Cambresis restores Savoy and Piedmont.
1564: the Bourbon block leaves the shape.
1589: Henry IV, first Bourbon, succeeds the last Valois.
1589: Henry III of Navarre becomes Henry IV of France and his lands join the crown.
1589: Navarre and Bearn stay a separate kingdom under the same king.
1601: France gives up Saluzzo in the Treaty of Lyon territorial exchanges.
1601: the Treaty of Lyon gives France Bresse, Bugey and Gex.
1620: Lower Navarre and Bearn are merged into France.
1620: Lower Navarre and Bearn become part of the kingdom.
1636: Cliopatria draws Lorraine inside the France shape from 1636.
1636: the Spanish reach Corbie in the war France declared in May 1635.
1640: Picardy and Alsace cells join the shape.
ledger.cp: Picardy and Alsace (holder not named by the pages opened)

ledger.x: 1641: Catalonia accepts Louis XIII.
1642: France seizes Roussillon; the Treaty of the Pyrenees makes it French in 1659 (occupation_end and gain below).
1648: the Peace of Westphalia gives France strategic places in Alsace.

1648: Breisach is given to France at Westphalia ('In the Peace of Westphalia in 1648, Breisach was de jure given to France'); returned to the Empire at Ryswick in 1697, recaptured on 7 September 1703, returned at Rastatt on 7 March 1714.
1652: Spain recaptures Barcelona and Catalonia leaves French protection.
1659: the occupation of Lorraine ends.
1659: the Treaty of the Pyrenees ends the war.
November 1659: the Treaty of the Pyrenees (signed 5 November 1659) turns the seizure of Roussillon into a cession.
1659: France gains Artois, Hainaut and Roussillon by the Treaty of the Pyrenees.
1663: French troops invade the papal Comtat Venaissin.
1663: the occupation is bridged as lasting that year; the page gives no end for it.
24 May 1667: Louis XIV crosses into the Spanish Netherlands in the War of Devolution; Charleroi falls first (2 June), Tournai, Courtrai and Oudenaarde by the end of July, Lille on 28 August.
1668: French troops invade the Comtat Venaissin again.
1668: bridged as lasting that year; the page gives no end for it.
February 1668: Conde's forces enter Franche-Comte on 4 February; Besancon and Salins surrender on 7 February, Dole on 14 February, Gray on the 19th.
2 May 1668: the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle returns Franche-Comte to Spain ('France withdrew from Franche-Comte and most of the Spanish Netherlands').
2 May 1668: the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle ends the War of Devolution.
2 May 1668: France keeps nine Flemish towns by the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle: 'he kept Armentieres, Bergues, Charleroi, Courtrai, Douai, Furnes, Lille, Oudenarde, and Tournai'.
1670: Louis XIV overruns the Duchy of Lorraine (mid-1670).
June 1672: the French overrun Utrecht (14 June, the council hands over the keys of the gates), Naarden (19 June) and Nijmegen in Gelderland (9 July).
1674: Louis evacuates Utrecht and Gelderland after the Dutch take Bonn in late 1673; 'the next year only Grave and Maastricht remained in French hands'.
1674: France overruns Franche-Comte in six weeks.
November 1677: the French capture Freiburg ('the French commander succeeded in capturing Freiburg in November 1677'); the Nijmegen infobox lists 'Lorraine, Freiburg, and Kehl' among the French gains.
1678: France takes Kehl, across the Rhine from Strasbourg ('In 1678, the city was taken over by France'; Vauban fortifies it in 1683).
March 1678: Louis captures Ghent ('captured Ypres and Ghent in early March', before the Dutch treaty of 10 August 1678; the sentence gives no year, which the date of the treaty supplies).
1678: Spain cedes Franche-Comte at Nijmegen.
1678: France gains Franche-Comte, Ypres, Maubeuge, Cateau-Cambresis, Valenciennes, Saint-Omer and Cassel at Nijmegen.
September 1678: France gives Charleroi back to Spain at Nijmegen.
September 1678: France returns Ghent to Spain at Nijmegen ('France returned Charleroi, Ghent and other towns in the Spanish Netherlands').
September 1678: France gives back 'other towns in the Spanish Netherlands' at Nijmegen.
1681: France seizes Strasbourg (30 September).
1682: the court settles at Versailles.
1683: the War of the Reunions opens in Flanders.
1684: France takes Luxembourg (June).
1684: the Truce of Ratisbon (15 August) guarantees the new borders for twenty years.
1688: France invades the Palatinate and the Rhine.
1690: Catinat wins at Staffarda and France holds Savoy and Nice.
1694: France takes Palamos and Girona.
1696: the Treaty of Turin ends the Savoy front; Pinerolo is handed back with its fortifications demolished.
1697: Ryswick (20 September) returns the Catalan places.
1697: Ryswick returns Lorraine to Duke Leopold.
1697: the Peace of Ryswick ends the Nine Years' War (20 September); 'French control over the entirety of Alsace was officially recognized'.
1697: France returns Luxembourg and Kortrijk to Spain.
1697: France returns Freiburg, Breisach and Kehl to the Empire.
1702: Imperial forces take Landau.
1703: French troops occupy Savoy after Victor Amadeus II changes sides.
1703: the French overrun the Piedmontese lands of Savoy.
1703: French forces retake Landau and capture Kehl and Breisach.
September 1706: Turin is relieved and the French lose Piedmont.
1707: the French occupy the County of Nice.
22 October 1708: Boufflers surrenders Lille to the Allies (the citadel follows on 9 December).
1713: Lille returns to France when the Dutch occupation ends.
1713: the French occupation of Savoy ends with the war.
1713: the French occupation of the County of Nice ends.
1713: Utrecht (11 April) cedes Ypres, Tournai, Menen, Veurne, Fort Knokke and Warneton to Austria.
1713: France gains the Principality of Orange (Utrecht).
1713: France gains the Ubaye Valley (Utrecht).

November 1713: Landau and Freiburg are lost by the Emperor Charles ('after the loss of Landau and Freiburg in November 1713, Charles finally made peace on 7 March 1714'); France keeps Landau at Rastatt and returns Freiburg, Breisach and Kehl.
1714: Rastatt (7 March) returns Breisach, Kehl and Freiburg; 'France retained Landau'.
1741: French forces hold ground in Germany east to 14.2 E.
ledger.cp: German lands (holder not named by the pages opened)

ledger.x: 1744: the German cells leave the shape.
ledger.cp: German lands (holder not named by the pages opened)

ledger.x: 1757: the French invade Hanover; the Convention of Klosterzeven follows after Hastenbeck.
1758: the French are driven out of Hanover and Westphalia (winter 1757-1758).
1760: the French capture Marburg in Hesse.
1762: France ends its war in Germany; the page gives no exact date.
1766: the Duchy of Lorraine passes to France.
1768: France occupies the Comtat Venaissin again.
1769: France conquers Corsica.
1774: the French occupation of the Comtat Venaissin ends (infobox 'French occupation:...
1789: the court returns to Paris.
1791: the Comtat Venaissin (Avignon) is annexed.
1791: the absolute monarchy becomes a constitutional monarchy.
1792: the monarchy is abolished and the First Republic proclaimed (21 September).

wars.name: First Barons' War
wars.outcome: Louis, called in by rebellious English barons, was defeated by English loyalists; naval defeat at Sandwich on 24 August 1217 and the Treaty of Lambeth (amnesty for the rebels) ended it.

wars.name: Conquest of Poitou (Louis VIII, 1224)
wars.outcome: French conquest of Poitou, La Rochelle, Limousin, Perigord and Quercy from the English crown; the English kept only the south-west (Gascony).

wars.name: Albigensian Crusade (royal campaign of 1226)
wars.outcome: Louis VIII took numerous Languedoc cities in 1226 (Avignon surrendered on 9 September) and left the crown holding much of Languedoc; the Treaty of Paris of 1229 ceded the sénéchaussées of Nîmes to the king (the Crown lands page names no others).

wars.name: Hundred Years' War
wars.outcome: Intermittent war 24 May 1337 to 19 October 1453: Calais lost 1347, Bretigny (8 May 1360) cedes increased lands in Aquitaine, Charles V reconquers 1369-1380, Henry V takes Normandy 1417-1419 and Troyes (1420) makes him heir, Joan of Arc and Charles VII turn…

wars.name: Burgundian Wars
wars.outcome: Charles the Bold was killed at Nancy on 5 January 1477; Louis XI seized Burgundy and Picardy and the Treaty of Arras of 1482 left the Burgundian lands reverting to the crown of France.

wars.name: Italian Wars
wars.outcome: France gains Milan and Naples briefly and loses both; at Cateau-Cambresis (3 April 1559) France 'retained Calais and the Three Bishoprics' and returned Corsica; the other provisions 'essentially returned the position to that prevailing in 1551'.

wars.name: French Wars of Religion (Henry IV's war for the throne)
wars.outcome: Henry of Navarre became king on the death of Henry III but the League 'was strong enough to prevent a universal recognition'; the Edict of Nantes and the Peace of Vervins (both 1598) ended the wars.

wars.name: Reapers' War (Catalan Revolt)
wars.outcome: Catalonia revolted in 1640 and accepted Louis XIII in 1641; 'During 1652, Spain recaptured both Dunkirk and Barcelona'.

wars.name: War of Devolution
wars.outcome: Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle, 2 May 1668: France withdrew from Franche-Comte and most of the Spanish Netherlands but kept Armentieres, Bergues, Charleroi, Courtrai, Douai, Furnes, Lille, Oudenaarde and Tournai (the War of Devolution page also lists Binche and…

wars.name: Franco-Dutch War
wars.outcome: Treaties of Nijmegen (August-September 1678): France gained Franche-Comte and the towns of Ypres, Maubeuge, Cateau-Cambresis, Valenciennes, Saint-Omer and Cassel and returned Charleroi, Ghent and other towns; the Dutch 'ended the war without losing an inch of…

wars.name: War of the Reunions
wars.outcome: France took Luxembourg in June 1684; the Truce of Ratisbon (15 August 1684) guaranteed the new borders for twenty years.

wars.name: Nine Years' War
wars.outcome: At Ryswick (20 September 1697) France returned Luxembourg and Kortrijk to Spain, Freiburg, Breisach and Kehl to the Empire and Lorraine to Duke Leopold, and 'French control over the entirety of Alsace was officially recognized'; the Treaty of Turin (29 August…

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession
wars.outcome: Utrecht (11 April 1713) and Rastatt (7 March 1714): France ceded Ypres, Tournai, Menen, Veurne, Fort Knokke and Warneton to Austria, gained the Principality of Orange and the Ubaye Valley, returned Breisach, Kehl and Freiburg and kept Landau.

wars.name: Seven Years' War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Paris (10 February 1763): 'France cedes its North American possessions east of the Mississippi River' and Louisiana west of it to Spain; France withdrew from Germany in 1762.

certainty.note: A small royal domain among great fiefs; no treaty or survey draws these frontiers and the Cliopatria shapes of 990-1205 are approximate (domain cores of 15,000-37,000 km2, with Aquitaine drawn in only 1139-1151).

Frontiers are approximate even where a treaty is dated: Normandy 1204, Nimes 1229, Bretigny 1360 and Troyes 1420, Arras 1435/1482, the Italian conquests and the Westphalia gains (Oct 1648) are dated but their lines are not drawn by the…
From the Treaty of the Pyrenees (Nov 1659) the frontiers are fixed by treaties (Nijmegen 1678, Ryswick 1697, Utrecht 1713, Rastatt 1714, Paris 1763).
